items.claim: The row's cited device "אֶל (oshb:Prov.3.5)" for 3:19's earth-founding clause is byte-false, and the inclusio word the row claims closes 3:18 is blank in the row's own text.
items.evidence: Prov.3.19 reads "יְֽהוָ֗ה בְּחָכְמָ֥ה יָֽסַד אָ֑רֶץ כּוֹנֵ֥ן שָׁ֝מַ֗יִם בִּתְבוּנָֽה" — its subject is יְֽהוָ֗ה, and אֶל does not occur in 3:19 at all; Prov.3.5, "בְּטַ֣ח אֶל יְ֭הוָה בְּכָל לִבֶּ֑ךָ וְאֶל בִּֽ֝ינָתְךָ֗ אַל תִּשָּׁעֵֽן", uses אֶל only as the preposition governing trust/leaning, in a verse outside 3:19, so the citation binds the wrong ref to a claim that ref does not support. Separately, Prov.3.18's own closing word is "מְאֻשָּֽׁר", sharing the root with the opening "אַשְׁרֵ֣י" of 3:13 (confirmed by direct comparison of the two verses' bytes) — the inclusio claim itself re-derives true, but the row's rationale and observed_substrate_signals print an empty span where that word belongs, a quote-loss defect the splice-not-hand-type discipline exists to prevent.

items.claim: The row's cited device "אֶל (oshb:Prov.3.5)" as the ground of the addressee's confidence at 3:25-3:26 is byte-false.
items.evidence: Prov.3.26 reads "כִּֽי יְ֭הוָה יִהְיֶ֣ה בְכִסְלֶ֑ךָ וְשָׁמַ֖ר רַגְלְךָ֣ מִלָּֽכֶד" — the acting noun is יְ֭הוָה, and אֶל does not occur in 3:26; Prov.3.5, "בְּטַ֣ח אֶל יְ֭הוָה בְּכָל לִבֶּ֑ךָ וְאֶל בִּֽ֝ינָתְךָ֗ אַל תִּשָּׁעֵֽן", is a different verse outside this row's own span where אֶל appears only twice as the preposition ('trust IN/toward YHWH... lean ON your own understanding'), never as the confidence-grounding actor the row attributes to it at 3:26.

items.claim: The row's five-verse prohibition run (3:27-3:31), its ketiv/qere and paseq disclosures, and its tov-min rival disclosure all re-derive true against the staged inventories and a fresh sweep.
items.evidence: The kq inventory confirms single-witness ketiv/qere at Prov.3.27, Prov.3.28, and Prov.3.30; the paseq inventory confirms the sole chapter-3 paseq at Prov.3.28; a fresh tov-mem skeleton sweep over the full book returns exactly 4 verses -- Prov.3.27, Prov.15.16, Prov.16.8, Prov.16.16 -- matching the row's claimed digit and named object exactly, and Prov.3.27's own text, "אַל תִּמְנַע ט֥וֹב מִבְּעָלָ֑יו בִּהְי֨וֹת לְאֵ֖ל ידיך יָדְךָ֣ לַעֲשֽׂוֹת", confirms the 'good FROM its owner' source-marked reading the row argues against the comparative rival.

items.claim: The row's cited device "אֶל (oshb:Prov.3.5)" as the divine actor of the four gnomic sayings at 3:32-3:35 is byte-false.
items.evidence: Prov.3.32 reads "כִּ֤י תוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְהוָ֣ה נָל֑וֹז וְֽאֶת יְשָׁרִ֥ים סוֹדֽוֹ" and Prov.3.33 reads "מְאֵרַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה בְּבֵ֣ית רָשָׁ֑ע וּנְוֵ֖ה צַדִּיקִ֣ים יְבָרֵֽךְ" — both explicitly name יְהוָ֣ה/יְ֭הוָה as the actor, and אֶל does not occur in either verse; Prov.3.5's אֶל (cited by the row) is the preposition in a different, out-of-span verse and does not recur as a divine-name device at 3:32-3:35.

items.claim: The row's exclusivity claim that the father-quoting-his-father structure is 'unique across 62 verses in this part' cites the part's total verse count, not a digit-bearing sweep of the claimed narrative device.
items.evidence: 62 is writer part P02's total size (Prov.3.1-Prov.4.27) from the tiling plan, not a count of embedded-quotation instances; no staged tool sweeps narrative-structure devices, so the universal 'unique' is asserted without the object-named, digit-bearing sweep the register rules require for exclusivity claims.

items.claim: The row's claim that the repeated imperative is 'echoed again at the head of 4.7' misdescribes the verse's actual opening, which is the separate clause "רֵאשִׁ֣ית", not the repeated imperative.
items.evidence: Prov.4.7 reads "רֵאשִׁ֣ית חָ֭כְמָה קְנֵ֣ה חָכְמָ֑ה וּבְכָל קִ֝נְיָנְךָ֗ קְנֵ֣ה בִינָֽה" — its first word is "רֵאשִׁ֣ית" ('the beginning/chief thing'), with the imperative recurring only as the verse's second clause; the repetition of Prov.4.5's opening, "קְנֵ֣ה חָ֭כְמָה", is real, but its position within 4:7 is medial, not initial.

items.claim: The row's front and back boundaries at 4:10 and 4:14 are each real, disclosed seams, and no petuchah, setumah, ketiv/qere, or paseq falls inside the span, matching the inventories exactly.
items.evidence: Prov.4.10 opens the third of the part's four bni-address openers (Prov.3.1, Prov.3.21, Prov.4.10, Prov.4.20, per the beni inventory); the pmarks, kq, and paseq inventories carry zero entries for Prov.4.10-Prov.4.13; Prov.4.14 opens a new prohibition with a distinct 'avoid the wicked path' object, confirming the row's stated seam.

items.claim: The row's rejected_alternative asserts that 4:16-4:19 'share one grammatical subject... running continuously,' but the row's own device_notes identifies 4:18-4:19 as an antithetic couplet contrasting the righteous with the wicked -- two subjects, not one.
items.evidence: Prov.4.18 reads "וְאֹ֣רַח צַ֭דִּיקִים כְּא֣וֹר נֹ֑גַהּ הוֹלֵ֥ךְ וָ֝א֗וֹר עַד נְכ֥וֹן הַיּֽוֹם" (subject: the path of the righteous, a new referent) and Prov.4.19 reads "דֶּ֣רֶךְ רְ֭שָׁעִים כָּֽאֲפֵלָ֑ה לֹ֥א יָ֝דְע֗וּ בַּמֶּ֥ה יִכָּשֵֽׁלוּ" (subject: the way of the wicked); the pronominal 'they' of Prov.4.16, "כִּ֤י לֹ֣א יִֽ֭שְׁנוּ אִם לֹ֣א יָרֵ֑עוּ וְֽנִגְזְלָ֥ה שְׁ֝נָתָ֗ם אִם לֹ֥א יכשולו יַכְשִֽׁילוּ", does not extend as one continuous subject through the antithetic pair the row's own device_notes flags.
